hypotheses_validated.claim: Root cause of the ~1 ms 32-thread dispatch: when a pool has as many threads as logical CPUs, any other runnable thread displaces a pool thread, and the displaced thread gets a CPU back only when some spinner reaches its spin_us deadline and goes to sleep (spinners never gave the CPU up). Each dispatch therefore took ~spin_us.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Original pool.c, 32 threads on 32 logical CPUs: p50 round trip 237 / 1031 / 3034 us at spin_us 200 / 1000 / 3000, i.e. it tracks spin_us. 16 and 24 threads: p50 0.7-0.8 us under the same load; 30 threads p50 1.1 us but p90 1033 us. Machine shared with other engineers' builds (~40% CPU), so this is the loaded regime.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Yielding spinners (SwitchToThread / sched_yield every 2 us, workers and the waiting caller) remove the spin_us-bound regime on Windows.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch bench (empty task, 5000 dispatches, interleaved A/B runs, loaded machine): 32 threads spin_us=1000 p50 1014-1031 us (original, and the new protocol with yields compiled out) -> 6.5-12.6 us; 16 threads unchanged at p50 0.6-0.7 us. Uneven-work regions (128 chunks, ~1 ms serial): 32 threads 1105 us per region (slower than serial) -> 60-88 us; 16 threads 74-76 us both. 64 threads (2x oversubscribed) spin 100 ms: p50 45-54 ms -> 0.81 ms. Pinned to one CPU (start /affinity), 4 threads, spin 200 ms: p50 2.1 ms original / 9.4 ms new protocol without yields / 0.7 ms with worker-only yields -> 12-15 us with caller yields too. Yield interval 1/2/4/20 us: 32-thread p50 6.5-8.9 / 8.1-8.4 / 12-16 / 28-43 us; 2 us chosen.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Per-worker condvars (instead of one condvar + mutex shared by all sleepers) make waking a sleeping pool faster and let hx_pool_for_n wake only its own threads.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: spin_us=0 pools, p50: 16 threads 54 -> 34 us, 32 threads 106 -> 57 us (Windows); WSL 16 threads 484 -> 302 us. for_n(2) on a sleeping 32-thread pool: 0.8-1.3 us vs hx_pool_run 54-86 us; the wake-all mutant raises for_n(2) to ~50 us and is caught by test_pool.

hypotheses_validated.claim: hx_pool_for_n is correct: chunks exactly once, tids < min(max_threads, n), exactly min(k, chunks) threads run concurrently, non-participants are never woken and never waited for, and arbitrary interleavings with hx_pool_run and idle gaps neither lose nor duplicate work.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_pool: 900 (threads, max_threads, n, chunk) coverage cases incl. INT_MIN/-1/0/1/INT_MAX-1 and n=INT64_MAX; concurrency barrier for k in {2,3,n-1,n} at 4/16/33 threads; 2700-op random mixed sequences at spin 0/3/200; passes on MSVC /O2, MSVC ASan, gcc -O2, gcc ASan+UBSan+LSan and gcc TSan (no race reports). Hand-made mutants (wake-all, no chunk cap, no spin-window refresh, no worker yield, no caller yield) are each caught.

hypotheses_validated.claim: hx_file_replace is atomic for concurrent readers and works while dst is open through hx_file handles, on Windows as on Linux.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_platform: 300 replaces of a 64 KiB file while a reader thread reopens and reads dst: 0 failed replaces, 0 torn reads, 0 open failures (Windows ~1000-1900 reads, Linux ~112000). On Windows MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING) fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED whenever any handle has dst open (even FILE_SHARE_DELETE ones); the POSIX-semantics rename (FileRenameInfoEx) succeeds and the old handle keeps reading the old data.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The T01 council's minor findings are fixed: empty env value on Windows, early timedwait timeouts, affinity-blind CPU counts (also on Linux for cores), unbounded env cache, locale-dependent hx_env_double, missing INT64_MAX boundary test, HEARTH_LOG whitespace in the test parser, sanitizer timing failures in test_pool.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: New test_platform run against the ORIGINAL platform_win.c fails 25 checks: empty var read as NULL (2), 2000 lookups 0.56 -> 221 ms after 30000 values of another variable, "0.25" -> default and "0,25" -> 0.25 under LC_NUMERIC=de_DE.UTF-8, timedwait early 2 of 24, and start /affinity masks 1/5/3 reported 32 cpus / 16 cores. New code: all pass (Windows 273 checks, Linux 244 with a localedef-generated de_DE locale via LOCPATH). The INT64_MAX boundary test uses a 1 GiB + 4 KiB request (committed, never touched) because a 10-byte read past INT64_MAX is rejected by the OS anyway; it kills the council's surviving mutant. test_pool turns timing checks off under ASan/TSan (or --no-timing); full ASan run 1746 checks / TSan --quick 1746 checks pass.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: The waiting caller should not yield (giving its CPU to another process only delays the next dispatch).
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Under external load the caller-without-yield variant was ~2-3 us better at 32-thread p50 (5.0-7.7 vs 7.4-11.4 us), but pinned to one CPU it made every dispatch take ~0.5-0.7 ms instead of ~14 us, because the caller held the only CPU its workers needed. A 20/50 us grace before the caller's first yield bought nothing measurable at 32 threads and made the pinned case 31/62 us. The caller yields every 2 us like the workers.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Yielding also fixes 32-thread dispatch on Linux (WSL2).
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: WSL2 gcc -O2, host loaded by other engineers: 32 threads spin_us=1000 p50 850-1060 us with yields vs 300-650 us without (both unusable: vCPUs are descheduled by the host and sched_yield only reaches the local runqueue; 24 threads were already 150-230 us). Yields still win where pool threads share a runqueue: pinned to one CPU 16 ms -> 16.6 us, 3 CPUs 4.0 ms -> 3.8 us, 64 threads spin 100 ms 34 -> 16 ms. 16 threads unchanged (p50 0.67-0.73 us).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) is enough for hx_file_replace on Windows (task text).
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: It fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED for as long as any handle has dst open, including hx_file handles that share delete access (measured: 250 ms of retries, then failure). Implemented the POSIX-semantics rename first and kept MoveFileExW as the fallback for volumes without FileRenameInfoEx; the fallback was exercised manually on the WSL 9P share (\\wsl.localhost\..., FileRenameInfoEx -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, MoveFileExW then succeeded) but has no automated test.

open_questions: Quiet-machine numbers were not obtainable: the machine was shared all session (other engineers' builds, 4-job mutation runs, a 23 GB Python job). The '32-thread within a small multiple of 16-thread' target is met under load only as 6.5-12.6 us vs 0.6-0.7 us (10-20x); on a quiet machine it should be closer, unverified.

Under external load, idle-spinning workers that yield can lose their CPU to other processes, so the next region waits for them: 16 threads, spin_us=1000, 20 us of caller-only work between regions: 33-41 us per iteration vs 29 us with the original pool. With the engine's POOL_SPIN_US=50 the new pool is at parity or better (100 us gaps: 136 vs 180 us). The amended hx_pool.h asks for the yields; the trade-off is recorded here.

Windows machines with several processor groups (> 64 logical CPUs): hx_num_cpus / hx_num_physical_cores ignore the affinity mask there (it only describes one group) and count every active processor. Not testable here (32 CPUs, one group).
